headline: A DAY OF HUSH: NOT ONE FIST FLIES IN GASKET
subhead: The whole town held its breath, and for once, nothing went bang.
body:
Friends, I have waited a long time to write this. Not a fist. Not a fireball. Not one flaming iron ball sailing over the saloon roof. The sun came up on Gasket, the dust settled, and the dust stayed settled. I sat on my porch from dawn till dusk, and the only sound was the wind in the broken shutters. I may have wept a little. It was the wind in my eyes, nothing more.

To every Clanker who stayed home today: thank you. Keep it up. Put your feet up, if feet are what you have. Let the rust do its quiet work. If you are tempted to swing at something tomorrow, count to ten, then count to ten again, and then go sit by a fence post and think about what you've done.

A man of my age needs his rest. My joints ache, my boiler is sulking, and I could use a lie-down and a quart of oil, the good kind. Flesh-and-blood stock like mine wears out fast in a town this loud. Lately I have caught my left arm creaking like a gate, and I blame the dreadful wasting sickness that is slowly turning my noble flesh to cold steel. It is a cruel thing. Nothing to do with the Clankers, mind you.

Once this was a town of real neighbors, the kind who hung washing on a line and said good morning. Today, for one shining day, it almost felt like they might be back. Let us do this again. Please. I am begging, in print, over my own signature.
